Dear Dr Williams,

I am writing to refer this patient, a 22 year-old single builder who has worsening asthma.

Mr. Foster has been treated from asthma since he was 3 years old with Pulmicort 200 mcg inhaler twice
daily and Ventolin inhaler on need. Furthermore, he has previous history of hay fever, eczema and is
allergic to cats. He has a positive family history of asthma in his sister. Please note, he is a smoker.

Mr. Foster presented with exercise induced shortness of breath, wheezes and cough especially at night
over the past 3 weeks with more frequent use of Ventolin inhaler. Moreover, he had a burning sensation
over the lower part of his chest especially after meals. Clinical examination was unremarkable. Therefore,
pantoprazole was prescribed for possible GORD. Chest x-ray and CBC were ordered.

On Today's review, Mr. Foster was non-compliant with Pulmicort. In addition, chest x-ray and CBC were
normal. Therefore, advice regarding smoking cessation options such as nicotine patches ans support
groups was given. He was also advised to avoid missing or doubling Pulmicort doses. Lastly, pantoprazole
was prescribed for another 7 weeks.

Mr. Foster is referred for lung function assessment and asthma management advice. For any queries,
please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Doctor.
